Sigma Advanced Systems Secures US$19.7
Million (Approx. ₹174 Crore) Order from North
American NATO Customer for critical 155 mm
Artillery Ammunition Subsystems
Fifth 155 mm milestone since May 2026 expands Sigma’s portfolio beyond shell bodies
and fuzes, advancing its transition from component supplier to integrated manufacturing
and engineering partner
Hyderabad, October 21, 2026: Sigma Advanced Systems Limited (“Sigma”), a global aerospace
and defence engineering and manufacturing company, today announced that it has secured an
order valued at US$19.70 million (approximately ₹174 crore) from a North American customer
serving the NATO defence ecosystem for the manufacture and supply of specialised ancillary
subsystems for 155 mm artillery ammunition. The order is scheduled to be executed by Q2 2027,
with manufacturing to be undertaken within the Sigma ecosystem.
The order marks Sigma’s fifth 155 mm engagement since May 2026, reflecting the steady
expansion of its capabilities across the artillery ammunition value chain. With shell bodies, filled
fuzes, advanced base-bleed shell technology, course-correction fuze collaboration and now
ancillary subsystems within its portfolio, Sigma is progressing beyond individual ammunition
component supply towards a broader manufacturing and engineering partnership across multiple
elements of the artillery round.
Global rearmament is reshaping the artillery ammunition
supply chain
The Russia–Ukraine war has highlighted the scale of artillery ammunition consumption in
high-intensity conflicts and the importance of sustained industrial capacity. NATO members and
allied governments have responded by prioritising inventory replenishment, longer-term
procurement and expansion of ammunition manufacturing capabilities.
The European Union’s Act in Support of Ammunition Production (ASAP), launched in 2024 with
€500 million in funding, was designed to address production bottlenecks and strengthen Europe’s
ammunition manufacturing base. NATO has also advanced initiatives focused on aggregating
demand, supporting multi-year procurement and expanding industrial capacity.

These developments highlight a broader shift in defence procurement. Meeting demand at scale
requires dependable manufacturing capacity across the supply chain, including the specialised
components and subsystems needed to support ammunition production.
For manufacturers such as Sigma, this creates opportunities to establish deeper positions within
international defence programmes. As customers scale production and introduce more advanced
technologies, the ability to support multiple elements of a product can become an important
differentiator in supplier selection and long-term programme participation.

The latest order is significant not only for its value, but also for the nature of the capabilities it
adds to Sigma’s portfolio. Shell bodies establish a foundation in precision manufacturing, while
fuze technologies and ancillary subsystems extend the scope of engineering, integration and
manufacturing expertise required across the ammunition system.
Subsystems and fuze integration can involve greater engineering content than standalone
components, including tighter coordination between interfaces, component performance,
manufacturing processes and quality requirements. This creates an opportunity for Sigma to
participate in more technically involved programmes and pursue a greater share of the value
generated across the supply chain.
As customers increase production volumes or adopt new ammunition technologies, a supplier
with experience across complementary components and subsystems can be better positioned to
address adjacent requirements. Sigma’s expanding portfolio provides a platform to pursue such
opportunities, subject to programme qualification, customer requirements and commercial
agreements.
Moving up the value chain
The strategic significance of the order extends beyond the addition of a new product category. It
supports Sigma’s broader ambition to build a more integrated presence in international defence
manufacturing, with engineering capabilities and production expertise spanning multiple elements
of the 155 mm ammunition ecosystem.
A wider portfolio can enable the company to build on existing manufacturing infrastructure, quality
systems and customer relationships while pursuing programmes with higher technical complexity.
It also creates opportunities to engage with customers earlier in the development and
industrialisation process, where relevant, and to support evolving production requirements over
the life of a programme.
The company’s recent engagements demonstrate a progression from filled fuzes to conventional
and advanced shell bodies, alongside collaboration on course-correction fuze

technology and the addition of ancillary subsystems. This combination strengthens Sigma’s
platform for pursuing adjacent requirements as international customers expand capacity and
diversify their supply chains.
The latest order is consistent with Sigma’s strategy of expanding its international defence
manufacturing footprint and building a more enduring role in specialised engineering and
manufacturing programmes.
Building towards a sustained international partnership
The current engagement provides another opportunity for Sigma to demonstrate its
manufacturing capabilities, quality standards and execution discipline in support of an
international defence customer.
As the programme progresses, its successful execution could support further engagement around
the customer’s evolving requirements. Any additional orders or longer-term supply arrangements
would remain subject to customer demand, programme performance and mutually agreed
commercial terms.
With international defence customers placing greater emphasis on reliable industrial capacity and
increasingly specialised manufacturing capabilities, Sigma intends to continue developing its
position across the global ammunition supply chain.
Commenting on the order, Sunil Kalidindi, CEO, Sigma Advanced Systems Limited, said:
“Global defence customers are looking beyond individual components to partners who can
support increasingly complex manufacturing requirements across the ammunition supply chain.
This calls for engineering depth, manufacturing consistency and the ability to deliver specialised
products at scale.
“This order builds on the capabilities Sigma has developed across the 155 mm segment and
marks a further step in broadening our role in international defence manufacturing. Our focus is
on building capabilities that allow us to participate in more technically demanding programmes
and respond to customers’ evolving requirements. We see this engagement as an opportunity to
strengthen our relationship with the customer and expand our contribution to the wider
ammunition manufacturing ecosystem.”
About Sigma Advanced Systems Limited
Sigma Advanced Systems Limited is an aerospace and defence engineering and manufacturing
company with capabilities spanning precision engineering, aerospace components, defence
systems and specialised manufacturing programmes for domestic and international customers.

The company is expanding its global manufacturing footprint, engineering capabilities and
international customer relationships across strategically important defence and aerospace
segments.
